We are recruiting for a fully funded PhD exploring the design of ambient intelligent systems to support multidisciplinary team meetings (MDTMs) in paediatric healthcare.

Multidisciplinary meetings are central to complex clinical decision making, bringing together different forms of expertise, evidence and knowledge about patients. Yet the information needed to make sense of a case is often distributed across records, systems and professional perspectives. Emerging generative AI and ambient intelligence technologies create new possibilities for systems that can follow the unfolding context of these discussions and surface relevant information at appropriate moments.

The PhD will investigate how such systems might be designed to become useful participants in multidisciplinary work without disrupting the collaborative practices through which clinical judgements are made. Building on formative ethnographic research with multidisciplinary care teams, the student will design, prototype and evaluate GenAI-based systems capable of recognising the evolving context of MDT discussions and providing contextually appropriate information to support clinical reasoning and decision making.

We are particularly interested in candidates with a background in HCI, Human-Centred Computing, Human-AI Interaction or a related area, and with an interest in developing and evaluating emerging AI technologies in real-world settings. Experience with generative AI or prototyping AI-based systems would be valuable, but we particularly welcome candidates interested in the human and collaborative dimensions of AI.

The PhD will be based at the University of Bristol and undertaken in collaboration with partners at Great Ormond Street Hospital (GOSH) and University College London. Funding is restricted to UK nationals only.
